Honestly,  I think this game is not worth it.  Yes, it is clear that it is a direct copy of the Starship Troopers theme with some tweaks, but that's not even why it isn't recommended to me.  In this game you drop in to a planet and just go ham on everything that isn't a Helldiver, but they don't give you a lot of options to do that.  it seems like they give you a lot of options of weapons and strategems (orbital attacks) but ultimately everyone just uses the same ones because if you want to play on a higher difficulty (need to in order to get better samples, which is needed to upgrade) then you have to use the only the ones that actually work.  Armor "choices" (light/Med/Heavy) barely do anything different outside of the bonuses that are on them which you can normally get on the better armor type, and the devs don't ever really fix the the actually balance issues.  There are more nerfs than anything and they penalize you for playing solo or with less than a full group, WHICH IS INSANE.  So if you want to play solo or with just one friend you get MANY more spawn in bugs/bots that will outswarm you, but if you play with 4 people you get LESS! spawn ins?   This makes no sense.  Also the spawn rate is SO glitchy and constantly has issues that they just aren't fixing.  This idea that "We die for Democracy!" joke in the game is funny, but ultimately is an absolute annoyance when the devs just try to make you die more than the allowance of the mission with every passing "update". The game is pretty much the exact same for every mission... just drop in objective/pew pew pew and get out (more pew pew pew than objective).  It gets very repetitive very fast.  Devs were supposed to add another enemy type (Bugs/Bots/???) and still haven't?  The amount of players has diminished a TON since opening because this level of nerfing/not fixing/only adding more things to pay $ for is all everyone is seeing and makes the game less and less fun.  If you don't have enough friends who have/get the game to play with you then don't get it as its mostly only fun if you and you're friends actually just have fun with it then actually try to take the game seriously like people do with most games. If you can get it on sale for less than $10, go ahead, that's the only way I see it being worth it.

[strike] Helldivers 2 had a lot of potential. Back in February, it looked fun, a little fresh, and kind of promising. I mean, I'm a simple man - I can take my flamethrower and show some alien bugs what it's like to live in hell, accompanied by three friends with a maniacal love of big, powerful explosions? Yeah, man, sign me up.
 
And it was kind of fun? I mean, yeah, I had 30 hours of fun. I scorched planets, posed in front of nuclear explosions, and beat the shit out of automatons with my friends every Saturday night. I had a blast, really, and that's pretty rare these days, especially with my case of playing video games every day for about 10 years. But as the first impressions wore off, things got a little sad. And as they say - you can only make a first impression once.

The people working on this game seem to have no idea what they're doing. Like they don't have a vision for their game or something. I think anyone who tried to get past the seventh difficulty without the weapons and stratagems that the game almost forces you to use felt this. The game started to feel unfair. 
At some point they started nerfing weapons, buffing enemies, and reducing the amount of stratagem slots available for higher difficulties (rip eruptor btw). Where is the fun in that? You can't kill Chargers with a flamethrower, you can't even damage Titan with a flamethrower, and yet they announce a full fire-based damage warbond for August. You can't kill a Titan with half of your stratagem weapons, you can't kill a Charger with different versions of the starter rifle(there're four of them). And there're a lot shit weapons you should not use even for normal enemies, they're just useless. And I don't even want to talk about automatons, trust me, it's even worse. FYI, starting with the eighth level missions on bugs, there will be dozens of Titans and Chargers, there will come a time when four-five Titans at a time will become trivial. It's not even funny after the first time. 

Oh, by the way, this game is published by Sony, and they actually thought it would be a good idea to make it mandatory to have a Sony account in order to play Helldivers 2. I'm not kidding, it was really bizarre shit, and now this game is not available on Steam for like... a hundred countries? Even Steam had enough of it and allowed people to get refunds despite their playtime and/or purchase date. Too bad I gave this game a second chance back then. 

As a conclusion I would like to mention their monetization system. Paywalling actual content behind $10 mini-battle-passes? And the game worth 30$? Yeah man, no thanks. By the way, shout out to the   d e g e n e r a t e s   who scream "BUT YOU CAN GET EVERYTHING FOR FREE!!!". Yeah, go get em tiger. Tho if you want to actually play this game like a lot and try all of what game has to offer you - than it will probably be waste of money. The core gameplay loop quickly becomes repetitive after a few hours. Missions typically involve destroying a few outposts and then extracting, which can get monotonous. When playing with random players, the overuse of airstrikes often means the mission is over before you’ve had a chance to fully engage, which takes a lot of the fun out of it. There doesn't seem to be much variation in the missions, and it can start feeling stale after about an hour.

This game has several issues. Changes are made frequently without being stated anywhere. There are bugs that haven’t been fixed for months, some even for over a year. Every major update somehow manages to hurt performance and causes crashes.

They also introduced more FOMO with the new Campaign system. In the past, everyone received the special (Stratagem) rewards regardless of whether they played during the event or not. Now, if you miss it by even one day, you won’t be able to get it for another several months.

The reporting system is also non functional in a game where Team killing is possible. You can gather a lot of samples, but if a teammate decides to go rogue at the very end, you’ve wasted all that time gathering it. Sometimes these players even work in groups.

They’ve made questionable changes in the past and haven’t reverted them, such as removing the ability to freely steer the hellpod. They also seem not to understand their own game when it comes to balancing. For example: why are enemy tanks replaced by warstriders, yet warstriders spawn as frequently as hulks despite being far more dangerous than tanks?

I hope to change this review to a positive one, but that doesn’t seem likely anytime soon based on the current direction of the game. I’m not expecting every issue on this list to be fixed, but at least some of them.

At this moment, the game, even when (despite bugs and hardlocks) playable, is not fun. Maybe someday. Who knows? I started to doubt it.

At launch Helldivers 2 was the most fun playing a multiplayer shooter I've had in over a decade.

Now it's a goddamn mess. Launch was incredible. Everything felt punchy and ridiculous, there was insane amounts of enemies, mad physics, ridiculously damaging and hilarious stratagems. Now approximately half or more of the guns I loved at the start have been neutered so badly they're borderline unusable.

Arrowhead, for the love of god let us have weaponry that works properly.

Stop nerfing everything based on its popularity, this is not an eSports PvP shooter.

Please understand that just because people are using the weapon most viable against the most dangerous enemies, it does not mean the weapon is overpowered. It means it is the best weapon to deal with the biggest threat.

When fighting Bugs, Chargers are your number one most dangerous foe. They're fast, hit like a truck and ragdoll the hell out of you. If you don't kill it fast, more come, and now have to deal with three or more at once. So when picking your loadout, the primary consideration is "what can kill a Charger quickly?"

Expendable Anti Tank does that. Quasar Cannon does that. Precision Orbital Strike does that. Eagle Airstrike does that. Eagle 500kg Bomb does that. 

What does not do that?
Every single primary weapon in the game. The giant orange glowing weakspot is basically like false eyes on a caterpillar. It is not a weakspot. The completely un-indicated, very armoured head is the instant kill spot. If you magdump into the 'weakspot' in its rear, the Charger will not die. 

Now apply that to practically every support weapon in the game too.

This is not the same when fighting Bots. In fact, every single Bot barring Factory Striders can be killed with a primary weapon if you hit the weak spot. This is not just good enemy design, it is good weapons balancing WITH THE ENEMY DESIGN IN MIND.

Arrowhead seems to fundamentally misunderstand the basic wants of their playerbase. If we want a greater challenge, we will play higher difficulties with more enemy spawns. 

We do NOT wish for our weapons to be made less effective.

The game has not been as fun as it was at launch for several months, due to the continued bone-head decisions made by the short-sighted and reactionary 're-balancing' with every patch.

Stop mucking with it, the golden goose is on life support.
The analogy of HD2 being a mechanic shop and you have a flat tire so they deflate the remaining tires for "balance" is SPOT ON. Save your time and invest it in something more rewarding.

Old review as of August 2024 during the "Escalation of Freedom" era, and much of it still applies now:
_________________________


I absolutely cannot recommend Helldivers 2.  May liberty guide your path elsewhere.

Why? 

Two words: wasted potential.



I have never seen such a horrible fall from grace since the launch of Helldivers 2.  This game was constantly the talk of the town and lauded for being leagues better than other modern games with a fair price point, an exceptional gameplay loop, an engaged community, and exciting room for expansion.  It was a phenomenon and strong Game of the Year contender.

Now, in August 2024, this game feels like the developers are playing practical jokes on the playerbase.

How did it fall apart?  It sure wasn't Sony.  It was Arrowhead themselves.

The top 3 issues:

1.  Enemies are way overtuned and oppressive, most player deaths feel like cheap-shots
2.  Weapons and tools to fight enemies are almost all underwhelming, anything useful is promptly nerfed by the devs
3.  No progression system, minimal significant updates, and nothing to look forward to for the foreseeable future

______________________

Enemies:


Fast, lethal, heavily-armored enemies swarm players on higher difficulties with very few options to fight back.  Whenever the playerbase discovers new weapons and tactics to deal with these overpowered and annoying heavy enemies, those useful weapons are nerfed with none of the other plentiful but weak options being buffed.  At this point, there is very little to effectively deal with the overabundant tanky enemies.

In the last 3 months, the devs released one of their infamous balance patches to fix this issue against both bug and bot enemies to "increase loadout variety."  They said they toned down how many heavy enemies would spawn on the map... but also increase how many non-heavy enemies spawn to compensate.  Sounds good, right?  Wrong.

Turns out they added a very rarely seen super-heavy variant of one of the bugs that takes twice as much effort to kill to almost completely replace the previous version we were already struggling with, and the number of these new enemies was NOT toned down.  Now when fighting bugs, you have more light and medium enemies then ever before, AND EVEN MORE TANKY HEAVY ENEMIES TO FIGHT WITH DOUBLE THE HEALTH.  WTF.

Ok, but at least the bots were made more fair from this change, right?  WRONG AGAIN.

Turns out the most challenging two bot enemy types (one that shoots rockets that ragdoll the player and the other that uses a ballistic shield and rapid-fire dead-on accurate machine gun) don't count as heavies and now are spammed WORSE THAN EVER BEFORE.

All of these changes came around the time that they also accidentally broke the enemy spawn system so that there are patrols everywhere that can spawn magically behind you and very easily call in 2-3 times more reinforcements almost instantly once they see you.  The tide of enemies is endless, and this makes players feel weak and outgunned.

With the latest update this week, they added EVEN MORE heavy enemies to both factions, and almost all of them bounce and ragdoll the player around with rockets and tentacles.  

___________________________
  
Weapons:

There has been a bizarre and ridiculous cycle of the dev team running spreadsheets on the most popular weapons and nerfing them until people stop using them.  In return, they sometimes slightly buff the worst weapons in some insignificant way thinking that will "balance" the game, which ends up accomplishing nothing.

This game has tons of guns and abilities to use on enemies, but over and over and over the most useful and fun have been nerfed like this is a PvP game.  Why the hell do the players ever need to be nerfed unless there are legitimate exploits being used?  It makes no sense.


Railgun efficiently taking out super-heavies?  *Not anymore. Armor penetration and damage heavily nerfed.

Slugger shotgun stunning devastator bots and doing big damage from mid-range?  *Nope, stun and damage both nerfed.

Eruptor explosive rifle dealing huge area damage with a fun shrapnel effect?  *No more shrapnel for you, damage gutted.

Quasar cannon quickly recharging and able to keep up with all the heavies?  *Now it's got a much longer recharge.

Flamethrower melting through armor and dealing with hordes of enemies quickly?  *Nah, now flames bounce off armor.

Flaming auto-shotgun clearing waves of bugs while still having ammo left for more?  *Time for an ammo nerf.


These are just some examples of weapons that people loved that were hit hard by nerfs for no real reason, one by one.  The overwhelming majority of weapons in the game do not do enough damage, do not have enough ammo, and are not fun to use.

The overwhelming hordes of overtuned enemies will overcome you on higher difficulties unless you use the very few weapons and stratagems that give you a fighting chance, and we seem to be losing more and more options with every "balance" patch.

________________________________

Content:

There have been plenty of small updates to the game since launch, but there has been absolutely zero progress made in the grand scheme of things.  The game launched in January, and in August we have:

- No new enemy faction
- No Helldiver progression system
- No weapon or stratagem upgrade tree whatsoever
- No weapon attachment options
- No armor skill upgrades or design customization
- Very few viable new guns or stratagems
- Lackluster amount of Helldiver voice options
- Barely any galactic campaign events (one planet is now a black hole, that's pretty much all that has happened)

SO MUCH IS MISSING.  So much time has been wasted on useless balance changes that have done far more harm than good.  In the meantime, the enemies have only gotten stronger with more powerful variants and the divers haven't gotten much at all to keep up.  

What is there to look forward to?  How long until a REAL major update?  


There seems to be no hope on the horizon for HD2.

The dev team has dug their own graves with "known issues" lists longer than the actual content updates, which is really pathetic.

Helldivers 2 is a game built on a solid and intriguing premise: fighting to protect Super Earth in a galactic war. The cooperative gameplay, combined with the satirical and militaristic tone of the lore, offers a unique experience that is both engaging and fun - at least initially. The idea of being a part of an elite force defending humanity against alien threats has great appeal and the chaotic, action-packed missions keep you on your toes.

However, as you dive deeper into the game, the cracks start to show. While the gameplay can be enjoyable for a while, the constant balancing and nerfing of weapons and stratagems begin to chip away at the fun. It becomes clear that anything even remotely effective or enjoyable will eventually be toned down, sometimes to the point of being unviable. It’s not a matter of if something will be nerfed, but when. This approach can make the game feel like it punishes players for finding effective strategies or getting too attached to certain tools.

The irony lies in the lore itself: despite Super Earth being capable of waging war on a galactic scale, the equipment provided to players often feels underwhelming or frustratingly weak. This drive for "realism" can detract from the sense of power and enjoyment that should come from being part of an elite force. Instead of feeling like a well-equipped soldier, you may find yourself grappling with gear that is more a hindrance than a help, which can sour the experience as time goes on.

One area where Helldivers 2 excels is in its approach to monetization. The Warbonds, or battle passes, are not time-limited, meaning that once they are released, they remain available for players to unlock at their own pace without any pressure. Additionally, premium currency can be earned through in-game activities, allowing players to enjoy the game’s full range of content without having to spend extra money. These consumer-friendly practices are a refreshing departure from the aggressive monetization strategies often seen in modern games, adding real value to the overall experience.

Overall, Helldivers 2 is a game with a great concept, but its execution leaves something to be desired. While it's certainly worth a try, especially for fans of cooperative shooters, be prepared for the inevitable frustration that comes with the game's approach to balancing.
